title: In progress of making an engine to make my first game
author: DaniShyland
selftext: Been a month or so since I started this project, any thoughts welcomed =\]. Still got placeholders...and have been agonizingly at the grind. :x. Engine is built using three.js and electron.

comments.author: Arumath
comments.body: That looks amazing! Could you give me some more details? What did you ask the AI to create? And what is this engine used for? Do you use it to create animations? How exactly does it work?

replies.author: DaniShyland
replies.body:
Thanks! I asked the AI to create tools so I could paint "freely" a level and potentially make an entire game and the physics behind it. What the ai made in terms of tools:  
\- Sky painter: Allows me to take an airbrush to the sky box  
\- Terrain deform: Allows me elevate the terrain freely with a brush  
\- Terrain noise: Allows me to color the terrain and upload a noise texture to paint with that colored texture  
\- Decals: Allows me to "sticker" the terrain like you see with the temporary path. Differs from terrain noise as terrain noise can only be use once per mesh  
\- Event Maker: Allows me to make cinematography and potential "events"  
\-  Character Editor: Allows me to edit per character loaded in animations, emotes, and save them to that specific character to be loaded when called. Allows me also to "Pose" which does a numerous amounts of things (originally only wanted to onion animations)  
\- UI Editor, lets me uploaded 2d images to edit the UI with and allows me to parent certain ui to make children such like when a person "joins your party".  
\- Parts lab let's disassemble the current model automatically  


As for what was procedural generated:  
Physics:  
\- Gravity, wind (which includes hair movement, and tree movement), extending certain bones, collision, some temp meshes (which I will be replacing), day and night  
Sounds:  
\- Wind, procedural noise steps based on what the next step of the terrain looked like  (this took a lot of prompting)  
Bug VFX:  
Butterflies, bees  


As for what the engine is for, it's to make games in this similar nature so if I wanted to I would know where everything is.

replies.author: Arumath
replies.body:
Thank you for your answer! If I’m not asking too much, could I ask you a few more questions?

What did you use to fix or refine the assets? Or how did you create them in the first place?

Could you explain in a bit more detail how you create the animations?

replies.author: DaniShyland
replies.body: Well some assets aren't ai generated, for the ones that are I use 3daistudio and prompt the image from front/back/sides to retexture them. Animations are taken from mixamo and other sources: retargetted, resampled, then from there the engine can segment them to form new animations by either slicing them, inserting frames, or changing the feeling of the animation by rendering a new frame then determining a flow from the pre-existing...say like I have a person flying, I would use pose mode to freeform the live skeleton placing the leg back, this would transform and reposition that animation to adhere to that new frame. The person person flying would kick their leg back, simulating swimming instead (the engine recursively generates every movement up to the frame asked of it using an algorithm, then oscillates between the animation)

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: Considered doing this myself just because I felt working in an engine you developed would be more intuitive and would only contain the things you actually wanted/needed instead of a lot of extraneous chaff to mentally block out. Can be tough though to reinvent the wheel with some of the more complex things like physics, lighting/shadow optimizations, etc. Good luck though. One of the better technical efforts I've seen .

replies.author: DaniShyland
replies.body:
It certainly is harder to reinvent the wheel. But it has its caveats where...you can control what you reinvent. And yes, optimization is even harder because most of this environment is limited to single threading and optimization techniques that take control of cpu gpu pipelines exist elsewhere where here you have the basic render pipeline in js. But I do have plans, this environment is just made to get a basis to export to another environment and is more for the workflow.
 
Regardless, thanks! =]

comments.author: Lumpy_Conference6640
comments.body: I haven't made any 3D RPGs, but this is definitely the future. I make engine and mod tools for all of my games, and it's changed the experience. AI can only take you so far, and don't get me wrong, that's like 80% of the way, but altering the placement and feel of a prop or gameplay dynamic- that fine-tuning- having the tools in place just makes it a deliberate experience.

replies.author: DaniShyland
replies.body: Absolutely agree. One of AI's strong points is tool production to help your workflow. I think it makes it a more tailored and personal experience, as well as being a little more controlled because you're still doing the heavy lift.
